decision.explanation: The question asks 'When was the Croatian money introduced?' and the sources provide two distinct valid answers depending on which version of the Croatian kuna is being referenced. Document D2S5 and others confirm that the kuna was first introduced on 26 July 1941 by the Independent State of Croatia during World War II. Additionally, D1S3 confirms the modern kuna was introduced on May 30, 1994, marking a separate transition from the Croatian dinar. Both dates are directly supported by the original sources and refer to distinct historical contexts.
